title: Rectilinear Propagation
ques: If you try to look at a candle flame through a straight plastic tube, you can see it. If you bend the tube, you cannot see the flame. What does this simple experiment prove about how light travels?

answer.content: This experiment proves that light travels in **straight lines**. It is called the rectilinear propagation of light. Because the light cannot bend around the curve of the tube, it doesn't reach your eye.

explanation: This demonstrates a core property of light using a classic scientific observation.

title: Shadows and Opaqueness
ques: Explain why a thick wooden door creates a dark shadow, but a clear glass window does not.

answer.content: A wooden door is **opaque**, meaning it completely blocks light from passing through, so it creates a dark shadow behind it. A glass window is **transparent**, meaning it lets almost all the light pass right through it, so it does not cast a dark shadow.

explanation: This tests the understanding of material properties (opaque vs transparent) and their effect on light.

title: Pinhole Camera Principle
ques: In a simple pinhole camera, light passes through a tiny hole and creates an image on the screen inside. What is special or unusual about the image that is formed on the screen?

answer.content: The image formed inside a pinhole camera is **inverted** (upside down). This happens because the light rays from the top of the object travel in a straight line through the hole to the bottom of the screen, and vice versa.

explanation: This applies rectilinear propagation to understand how a basic optical device works.
